questions.question: How much electricity did Illinois generate from nuclear power over calendar year 2025, the twelve months summed, in MWh?
questions.answer: Illinois generated 97,670,262 MWh of nuclear electricity in calendar year 2025. That is the sum of 12 monthly values, January to December 2025, in state_generation_mix_monthly (derived, entity eia:IL, variable net_generation_nuclear_mwh). Months are calendar months. The monthly values ran from 7,363,785 MWh in February 2025 to 8,832,211 MWh in January 2025.

questions.question: On the battery page, how much did a 4-hour battery with perfect foresight earn in total at ERCOT's hub average in September 2026, in USD per kW?
questions.answer: A 4-hour battery with perfect foresight earned 6.87 USD/kW in total (energy plus ancillary services) at ERCOT's HB_HUBAVG in September 2026. The table gives this as 6.868615 USD/kW, which is 6,868.6153 USD/MW (battery_stack_monthly, derived). The month is a local (America/Chicago) month. All 30 of its 30 days were held (battery_stack_monthly). This is a perfect-foresight upper bound for a price-taking battery. It includes no capacity payment.

questions.question: What was the highest 5-minute battery discharge on CAISO's grid on 10 November 2026 (Pacific time), in MW?
questions.answer: The highest 5-minute battery discharge on CAISO's grid on 10 November 2026 (Pacific time) was 7,682 MW (caiso_battery_storage, variable batteries_mw). It occurred at 4:50 pm Pacific (00:50 UTC on 11 November). This is the maximum of 288 five-minute readings for the Pacific day. Positive values mean discharging.
